name: Clock times that wrap at midnight
brief:
A futures desk trades nearly round the clock, so its scheduler works in minutes after midnight, 0 to 1439. Write `class SessionTime` with an `explicit SessionTime(int minutes)` that wraps any whole number into 0 to 1439, and `int minutes() const`. Then write three free operators. `t + m` is the time `m` minutes later (`m` may be negative). `b - a` is the number of minutes forward from `a` to `b`, 0 to 1439. `a < b` compares the times within one day.

23:50 plus 20 minutes is 00:10, so `(SessionTime(1430) + 20).minutes()` is 10. Going forward from 23:50 to 00:30 takes 40 minutes, so the answer to `SessionTime(30) - SessionTime(1430)` is 40.
constraints: `SessionTime t = 5;` must not compile: the constructor is `explicit`.
hint: In C++ `%` keeps the sign of the left side, so -30 % 1440 is -30. Add 1440 and take `%` again.

examples.note: Past midnight the clock starts again at 0.

how: Submit runs 14 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value. The last only compiles `SessionTime t = 5;` and expects it to be refused.
notes: Wrapping once, in the constructor, keeps every `SessionTime` inside 0 to 1439, so the operators can trust it.
`((m % 1440) + 1440) % 1440` is right for negative `m`; `m % 1440` alone can be negative.
`b - a` reuses the constructor's wrap, so a time just before midnight to one just after gives a small number.

planted.slip: Uses % alone, so a negative minute count stays negative.
The difference is not wrapped, so a span across midnight comes out negative.
Wraps by one day only, so a count more than a day out of range stays out of range.
